utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-95-16-PT, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Before I begin with the examination of the witness, would you please allow me to address a question to the Trial Chamber, and could the witness leave the courtroom for a moment while I address that question to the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. President, my question has to do with the documents which the Prosecutor intends to use in today's cross-examination. Actually, yesterday we received two documents from the Prosecutor which he intends to use in his cross-examination. The first document was given to us prior to the beginning of the hearing and before the witness was brought into the courtroom, and we consider that quite appropriate. However, as regards the second document, the Prosecutor gave it to us immediately after the end of the hearing, that is, after the witness had started testifying and had taken the solemn declaration. Clearly, the document was given at that very point in time so as not to enable the Defence counsel to ask the witness anything about that document before the Prosecutor. As the Defence counsel, I have had enough time to study the document, but I was not in a position to confront the witness with it. My question to the Trial Chamber is as follows: Is such a disclosure of documents on behalf of the Prosecutor in accordance with the Rules of Procedure or, rather, is it permissible for the Prosecutor to prevent the Defence from asking the witness about documents in the possession of the Prosecutor, the aim being to surprise the witness with a document which he was not in a position to see before? If Your Honours consider such a procedure to be in accordance with the Rules, I apologise if this is due to any misunderstanding on my part. If not, would I be allowed to discuss this document with the witness for ten minutes, at least, prior to the examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I give the floor to Mr. Terrier, may I ask whether we could also be given these two documents? Before making a ruling, we have to read those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So we will concentrate on the documents to which Counsel Par has just made an objection. He said "the second document", which, Counsel Par, could you please specify which one is the second document, the one --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The first document is a letter to the International Tribunal, and we have no dispute over that, and the second document with the signature regarding the confiscation of weapons and so on, a report on inventory taken by the inventory commission, with the annexes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, this is the first one. So the first document is a letter by Ljubica Kupreskic to the International Criminal Tribunal, the first one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, and we're not disputing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The one we are disputing is the report on inventory taken by the inventory commission. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good. Could I ask Mr. Terrier to comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. First of all, I would like to say that by serving the document prior to the beginning of the cross-examination and even before the end of the examination-in-chief, and by giving Mr. Par one night to think it over, I think that we perfectly complied with the directives edicted by this Tribunal. Secondly, when it comes to the letter written by the witness to the Prosecutor in The Hague, that shouldn't raise any problem whatsoever. Thirdly, with regard to the report by the inventory commission, I do not have much information as to the nature and the purpose of such a commission, but by serving this document to the Defence, my primary concern was to ask the witness whether she recognised the signature at the end of this document and the name of Vlatko Kupreskic. I didn't intend to ask the witness, because I don't think she would know that, whether she knew anything special as to the purpose of the commission, as to the results obtained by the commission. The main purpose of serving the document to the Defence was for the witness to recognise or for failing to recognise the signature of her husband. Besides, Mr. Par has not completed examination-in-chief. He is therefore perfectly able to ask all questions he deems useful on this report or on anything else. This is what I had to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Fully appreciating the observations by my learned friend, Mr. Terrier, if the question has to do with the signature alone, then I have no objection. At the same time, however, my question was of a principle nature so we should know in the future what exactly is the position of the Trial Chamber regarding the disclosure of documents. But I would stress, once again, that if it is a question of recognising the signature, I withdraw my complaint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Now, our ruling, of course, is of a general nature, because you raised the question of principle. I understand that you accept, in light of what the Prosecutor just said, his explanation. He will confine himself to asking questions about the signature of the witness's husband, so therefore you are not raising any question. As a matter of principle, however, we agree with your position. We feel that the Prosecutor should disclose these documents as soon as possible, not at the very last minute, because this may delay our proceedings. In any case, if the Prosecution is unable to disclose such documents as soon as possible, it is only fair for the Defence counsel to have some time to discuss a new document with the witness in private. So in future, if the same occurrence arises, then we will allow the Defence counsel to take some time to discuss any matter relating to a particular document which has just been disclosed, or has been disclosed a short time before the testimony, to discuss it with the witness. So we will proceed this way in the future. For the time being, we can resume our proceedings, and I would like to ask the registrar to bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Kupreskic. May we begin? During today's examination, we will mainly be dealing with a certain number of documents. Yesterday, in the course of your examination, you said that during the conflict, Vlatko Kupreskic did not have a rifle. My question is: When he was arrested, was a rifle seized from him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, when he was arrested, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court where that rifle came from, when and how he gained possession of it, and why he needed it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That rifle was purchased upon my initiative because of frequent burglaries in our house and our shop, and I was the one who initiated the purchase of such a rifle because I was often left alone with the children. After the cease-fire was signed in May, a burglary occurred into my house. I was alone with the children. Vlatko was away on business at the time, and when he returned, I told him about it, and I said that he should get a weapon, because I was afraid to stay alone, as our house is rather isolated. Everything around it had been burned. However, Vlatko did not follow my advice on that occasion, but after another burglary in our shop, when a large amount of goods were stolen, in January '95, he went to the military and asked them to give us a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, could I show the witness this document, and I have copies for Their Honours, the Prosecution, and the registry. The original for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit will be Defence Exhibit 35/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mrs. Kupreskic, you are familiar with this receipt, so could you tell us what it certifies and where it comes from?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a card on the basis of which weapons were issued. We can see here that the name is Vlatko Kupreskic, the date is 17th of January, 1995, when he was issued this rifle. The rifle was issued by Mr. Smiljko Cevozic, and this card was deposited in the registry in our shop on the same day that the rifle was issued. This is evident from the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Does this mean, when a rifle is issued, that such a document is issued at the same time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can we see what kind of weapon it is?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know much about weapons, but I can read what it says: AP 2223. It probably means an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And what else was issued?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Three magazines of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. So we are finished with that certificate. You mentioned that there were some burglaries in your shop and home, so I'll show you another certificate for you to look at and tell us what the origins of that document are, with the help of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D36/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mrs. Kupreskic, this, too, is a familiar document for you, so could you briefly tell the Court what kind of certificate it is, who issued it, and what does it certify?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At my personal request, this certificate was issued by the police administration of Vitez, and the burglaries that took place were registered. The first one occurred on the 17th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: 1994, in our family house. The second one occurred in September 1994, and the third in February 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let us refresh our memory: When was the rifle issued?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In January 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So the reasons were these burglaries, as you have told us?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could I ask the registry to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P329, P329, a certificate on mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Until we find that document, let me tell you that it is a document which says that Vlatko Kupreskic, from the 16th of April, 1993, was assistant commander for health in the Vitez Brigade. So could you look at this certificate and comment on the accuracy of the statements it contains. Have you received a copy?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My husband never had a certificate of this kind, nor have I seen it before I was shown it by counsel. It is not correct, what it says here, that he was assistant commander for health from the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What is not right? The title that he held, or the date?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was not even mobilised then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And when was he mobilised?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Around the beginning of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And to what post was he assigned?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was assigned to the position of driver in the medical corps, because an order arrived to confiscate Vlatko's white Mercedes which he owned at the time. During the general mobilisation, Vlatko was mobilised by force, and he used that vehicle as a driver working for the medical corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know whether Vlatko asked to be issued such a certificate for some particular purpose?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. If he had asked for it, I would have probably seen it. I've never seen it before, nor did he request such a certificate to be issued to him, and I really don't know where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go on. Did any member of your family, or acquaintance, on the basis of erroneously-entered data on participation in the war, acquire the right to certain shares?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let me show you a few documents that I received from you, but we would like to show them to Their Honours. You know that I have three so-called certificates on the salary for members of the armed forces. I should like to ask you to tell me briefly, with regard to each of those certificates, to whom they apply, when the person mentioned was born, to what extent she participated in the war, and whether you personally know that person and can confirm whether the data indicated are correct. Do you have the certificate before you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This certificate applies to Ana Topic, born in 1928, which can be seen from her personal registration number. According to this certificate, she was a member of the armed forces for 49 months, which is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: For 49 months; a person born in 1928 would hardly have been a member of the armed forces. Do you know her in person?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know that she's not very well physically, and she is my brother's mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let us go through two more certificates that I have here of a similar nature.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit will be D37/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mrs. Kupreskic, very briefly, to whom does this certificate apply?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It applies to Ljubica Frljic, born in 1928, and it says here that she too was a member of the armed forces for 45 months, which is not true. This is actually my mother. She has been sick for 30 years. She's under medication. She can hardly walk. So this is really not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how can you tell the age from the registration number of the person?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: We have one further certificate of this kind.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D39/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you comment in the same way on this certificate?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It applies to Miroslava Jonjic. She is a refugee from Zenica. She's the mother of a worker that I employed. It says here she participated for 45 months and acquired a salary on that basis. She was born in 1937, which can be seen from her personal registration number. This lady died a couple of months ago. She was of poor health.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: A few more words about her. How can you see that it is not correct that she was in the armed forces? How do you know that? That she was sick, you mean?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: That she participated in the armed forces for 45 months, how can it be true?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know her personally. She was really sick. She was immobile. She couldn't move. She was bedridden.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let us go on to the next document. You said, Mrs. Kupreskic, that on the 15th of April, on the eve of the conflict in Ahmici, you took your driving test. Now I shall show you another certificate confirming this. In view of the fact that what you are going to see is also a certificate that you obtained and gave to me, let us not dwell on it too long. Just tell Their Honours what the certificate says or, rather, who issued it and how.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit D40/3.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This certificate certifies that I, Ljubica Kupreskic, took my driving test on the 15th of April, 1993, at 16.00 in Vitez in the auto motoring club in Vitez. This certificate was registered in the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I would now like to ask the Registry to give us Defence Exhibit D12/3, which is the minutes on damage to the house or report on damage to the house of Vlatko Kupreskic. D12/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that on the 16th of April, '93, certain damage was inflicted on your house and that some things were stolen from your house. Did you apply for compensation for this damage or, rather, are you familiar with this record that you have?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was this record drawn when you applied for damages?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Briefly, what kind of damage is indicated here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This record was drawn on the 15th -- no, the 5th of April, 1995, and at that time the things taken away and damaged or, rather, the merchandise taken away, so I did notice. So in 1995, we already said that the entrance door was damaged, as you can see from here, that a large part of merchandise was damaged. All the bills and receipts were stolen. Then there was valuables, jewellery or, more specifically, a necklace, a golden necklace, which was a wedding present to me from Vlatko's parents. So the commission came out and wrote it all down. So windows were damaged, the heating system was damaged, roof tiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right. Let us then proceed to the next document, or two more. The next document is a certificate of the Centre for Social Work in Vitez. You were also the one who gave it to me. So will you tell us, what is this certificate? Who issued it, and what does it satisfy about?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was issued by the Centre for Social Work to certify that our family, as of the -- on the 1st of May, 1993, we were refugees in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: That was the period of time when you came from Rovna to Vitez. When you came there, did you immediately report to the centre? What was the procedure at the time about registering refugees?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. Someone from door to door and making the -- compiling the list of refugees, and thus then putting us on the record in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. We have more or less finished with these documents. Only two or three short questions more.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me. This document was Exhibit D41/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Only a few brief questions related to some character statements which we already gave the Prosecution. Let us see how they came about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, on what terms was Vlatko with the Muslims after the war, after the conflicts? Did the Muslims that you had contact with accuse him of some infamous role in the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Vlatko, with all people and in particular with the Muslims, Vlatko was on the same terms as before the war. And with all the people that I had to do something with, and I had to deal with a number of people, I had contact with a number of people, Serbs including, nobody said anything against Vlatko. Everybody was surprised when Vlatko was indicted. They knew him well. They knew he was a good businessman, and he always helped people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Where did you talk to them, where did you meet them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I mostly talked to them in Ahmici, in front of my house, in the shop in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did you ask them something specific from them? Did you ask them to come to the Tribunal or write some statements? What was their response? What did those conversations look like?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. When you told me that the Tribunal permitted us to take down some character statements, I went to see my neighbours, asking them to write down a statement or come here to the Tribunal. Some of them did write it down, except that people want to be protected. They have all some problems. Some of them would be ready to come to testify as to the character of Vlatko Kupreskic, but they are afraid to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. It is clear now. I have here a list of people who wrote down these character statements. We submitted them to the Prosecutor's office in time, and I should now like to show you the list of these people. I don't want you to read out all these names, because this is a public session. I only want to ask you which one of these persons is a Croat and which one is a Muslim? We have numbers here, so will you please tell us just that number so and so is a Muslim and number so and so is a Croat?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, will you please help? This document is a certificate of the municipal department that these persons were contacted to, and we shall attempt to enter it into evidence subsequently.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't want to take too much of your time, so number 1, this is a person of Muslim ethnicity. Number 2, also Muslim ethnicity. Number 3, Muslim ethnicity. Number 4, Muslim ethnicity. Number 5, Serb. Number 6, Serb; 7, a Muslim woman. Number 8, a Muslim woman. Number 9, a Serb. Number 10, a Muslim; 11, a Muslim; 12, Muslim; 13, Muslim; 14, Muslim; 15, Muslim. Number 16, Muslim. Number 16 (sic), Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Kupreskic. I have no further questions, and I should like that these D31/3 to number D41/3 be admitted into evidence as Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The last document will be marked D42/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, D42/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, the interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes. As to the last document, D42/3, I'm wondering whether this document can be tendered into evidence today. There is only one list of names, whilst there is no indication as to the relevance of this document, given the facts the accused is accused of in this trial or when you think of the testimony of Mrs. Kupreskic today. I would like to have this document together with statements which are apparently announced but have not been provided yet. I do not think that the last document, D42/3, could be usefully tendered into evidence. I do not have any objections as to the other documents which were provided today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I agree. I withdraw my suggestion for 42/3, and we'll submit it in the end with a list of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So therefore all the other documents are admitted into evidence except for D42/3, which will probably be submitted into evidence later on with the other accompanying documents. Yes, Counsel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I should merely like to inform you that Mrs. Slokovic-Glumac will also ask some questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. This is for cross-examination. All right, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kupreskic, I understand that you work for the Sutre company.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was there between '92, end of '92, until the war. And then after the war, I went back to work there and became even more active there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Will you tell us if at that time Mirjan Kupreskic was also there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mirjan Kupreskic was also there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Where did he work before the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Before the war, he worked at the outlet in Pirici, and then some 15 days before it, he moved to Vitez. So for a while before the war in '93, he moved to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who worked with him at the warehouse at the time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Ivica Covic was with him at the warehouse in Covici, so Mirjan moved from that warehouse to Vitez because we opened there another business outlet there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did Ivica Covic go on working in the warehouse until the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And after the war -- that is, in 1994, when the cease-fire was signed -- in 1994, did Mirjan Kupreskic continue to work there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Mirjan Kupreskic continued to work there, and I saw him every day there because I did paperwork there, and he was downstairs in the sales department.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Witness. I am Franck Terrier. I'm one of the prosecutors, as you know, and you know that I'm going to ask you a series of questions following the examination-in-chief. First of all, could you tell us about professional activities of your husband, and about yours as well, prior to the war, in 1992 up to April 1993. Could you also tell us how the business evolved after the war, you know, I'm talking about the business run by your husband. How did that develop?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I ask you to speak slower? You asked very many questions. I do apologise, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I am going to attempt to comply with your wish. On several occasions you mentioned the store, the Sutre store, that company that you had; could you tell us how the company was organised? Who was the owner of it, and what was the exact part played by your husband in that company?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Ivica Kupreskic was the owner of the Sutre company, both the manager and the owner, and my husband worked together with Ivica Kupreskic as a professional, as an expert, because he had graduated from the faculty of economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What was your husband supposed to do within that company? What was his role?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was responsible for commercial affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific as to the purpose of that company? What were you trading in? What was the company trading in? I'm having in mind the months if not the years prior to the war, so before April '93.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time the company was trading in wholesale and retail trade in foodstuffs, and textiles to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: On several occasions before this Tribunal a shop in Vitez was mentioned. Who was the owner of that shop?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Ivica Kupreskic. It was one company with two units, with two outlets. One of them was in Pirici and the other one was in Vitez. So it is one company.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So let's be quite clear: The Sutre company, whose owner and director was Ivica Kupreskic, had its seat in Ahmici and Pirici, but also had an outlet in Vitez? Is that so? Was your husband working more in the Vitez outlet? Would he work more frequently in Vitez than in Pirici?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. He spent just as much time over there as over here, because sometimes he worked until midnight putting papers in order and so on and so forth. I have an office at home, even. It just depends on the kind of transaction, on business partners. They would come, perhaps we would meet in Vitez, conduct negotiations, and then he would go to fetch the merchandise, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What became of that company during the war? As of April 1993, what happened to the company?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In April 1993, there was merchandise in this company. All that we had, at that time, we had invested in merchandise. That company, when the conflict broke out, was closed down until the cease-fire was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You mentioned investment you made. Do you think of yourself making such investment, you and your husband, or was it the company that was investing? Did your husband invest his own money into the Sutre company?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: These funds came from the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In the period following the cease-fire, what happened then? As of then, how did the business evolve? How did your husband's relations with Ivica Kupreskic evolve?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me see, sometime in May, in early May, the company reopened. It was very difficult. It was very dangerous to go and bring the merchandise in. I mean, the roads were dangerous. It was difficult to set the company in motion again and start developing it, but somehow we all joined in, and we were managing somehow to do it, and Vlatko and Ivica Kupreskic were on correct terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Isn't it true to say that at some point in time, your husband -- and probably you, yourself, as well -- became independent in relation to Ivica Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, in August 1994, we founded a private company called Modus, and I'm its manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So you created this new company called Modus. Was it a company with the same purpose as the former one, which was managed by Ivica Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was the same branch of activity, and it is to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What happened to the company run by Ivica Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they continued in business. They still do the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So you're basically competitors, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is irrelevant. I take this question -- right, I'll give you an answer. Ivica Kupreskic has a shop, and he still sells foodstuffs, but he has expanded his activity, and he also engages in trade in other types of merchandise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it true to say that your company -- and I'm now speaking of the Modus company -- as of August 1994 up till today imports into Bosnia goods which it then sells to other intermediaries? So basically you have an import business, and then you have wholesale trading? Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And how do you go about it? How do you import goods? How do you manage contacts with sellers abroad?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We do not import anything from foreign countries. Our merchandise -- our supplies come mostly from Herzegovina, so we are second-hand in delivery of it. Sometimes we order it by telephone. Sometimes our representatives go there directly to our suppliers, conclude the contract, orders. So the merchandise will have a driver. He goes, ships it in, we store it there. Then, when we sell it, then we go and purchase a new lot. That's how it goes on and on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: How many employees does the Modus company have today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Modus employs ten people at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you run the business yourself, personally?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As much as I can, since I'm all by myself, that I'm both guardian and mother, and wife of an unjustly accused person. He has no father, no brother; I'm all alone. But I do have an accountant, and he keeps books, on a day-to-day basis. I have two brothers who also work with me, so that -- but it's hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you give us some information as to the yearly turnover of the Modus company? Approximately so -- I'm not the, you know, Inland Revenue. Just to have an idea.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The amount of money that passes through the company? Well, don't you think it's a business secret?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Keep your professional secret for yourself, then. Let's talk about the shippers, or people who would transport goods. Do you employ Fadil Sipcic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Tomo Simic, who is a Serb, works for me, and Fadil Sipcic never worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm now going to mention your husband's activities prior to April 1993. It looks as though the Sutre company then mainly imported goods from Croatia and sold such goods in Central Bosnia. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In order to buy goods in Croatia, it would happen that Ivica Kupreskic and your husband would go to Croatia; is that so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course. How else would they buy the goods?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how often, how regularly, your husband would go to Croatia at that time? And the period I have in mind is late 1992, early 1993.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That depended on demand. Sometimes he would go three times a week, sometimes once a week. That depended. If we sold out the goods quickly, then he would have to go as often as three times a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that your husband's trips to Croatia were then at least once a week?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Once, sometimes two times, sometimes three times. It depended on the demand for goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Would your husband usually go to Croatia alone, or was he together with someone else?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He usually went with Ivica Kupreskic or with me, personally, so that I travelled frequently in that period with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So if you would go with him to Croatia, what kind of contracts or agreements would he conclude? What kind of contacts would he mostly have in Croatia when he made such trips?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When contacting larger firms, Ivica would travel with him. However, to purchase clothing, like jeans, we would usually purchase them at the large market in Split. I would go there by passenger car, because we didn't have so much demand for clothing, because I mentioned that we dealt in clothing on the side, on a minor scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: How long does a trip to Croatia take, madam? How many days did you have to spend away from home?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Usually two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Where did your husband use to spend the night, the night away from home, since the journey would take two days?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Most frequently we would spend the night with Radislav Simovic. Sometimes, in Split, with an old lady who was renting rooms. I personally spent the night there with this old lady in Split twice. And we went to stay with Radislav Simovic for our annual holidays.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you mean that as far as business trips were concerned, which were basically once or more a week, your husband would spend the night at Radislav Simovic's place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It depended. Sometimes in Split, sometimes at Radislav's place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But you mean by that that it was very customary for your husband, very frequent for your husband to spend the night at Radislav Simovic's, say in the season period, or as well in the off-season period?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In September 1998, a witness testifying under the pseudonym of "WT" testified in front of this Tribunal, and the witness said that in October 1992, he'd seen your husband, Vlatko Kupreskic, he had seen yourself and a third person, a male, unloading a Yugo vehicle in front of your house, and there were weapons which they were unloading. This witness was heard on the 24th of September, 1998, and this was in front of your house. According to the witness testimony, this was happening in October 1992. What does this make you think of? What do you think of this witness testimony?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I deny that, 100 per cent, because it is not true. We would often unload goods when we didn't have room in the warehouse, so we would unload them in the garage into the house. We are still doing that to this day. But that we unloaded weapons, that really is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When your husband went to Croatia on business trips, which vehicle would he usually take to go?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Usually the Yugo 45, because the road was not very good. Ivica owned a Mercedes in those days as well, but because the road was not in very good condition, we would use this smaller vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it possible that sometime in October 1992 your husband brought back from Croatia goods or items that could be mistaken for weapons by a witness located some 50 metres away from the location where you were?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it's not possible. Nobody could ever think that weapons were brought into my house, and they were not, until I insisted on this rifle for the purpose of protecting myself from burglars. You can check on the spot. In the attic there are cigarettes, in the garage there are other goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Were you ever helped by a third person, by a man, when you had to unload the Yugo, you and your husband? Did it happen that somebody helped you to carry goods inside the house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There are workers whose duty it is to carry the goods. Neither Vlatko nor I carried the goods. I'm a woman, after all, and Vlatko is not allowed to strain himself, because of his health.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: During that period of late '92, early '93, given the circumstances prevailing at the time, did it happen that your husband bought military-type items? I'm having in mind not only weapons but also military uniforms, or any other equipment used by the army, that he got from Croatia. I also have tents in mind, for instance, or whatever equipment of that type.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not remember that. I don't remember that they purchased any goods of that kind, nor did I see such goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But you don't rule that out? You don't remember it, but you don't rule that possibility out, do you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know. I never saw it, and if I didn't see it, it probably never was purchased. Surely I would have seen such things if they had been purchased.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher's help for Prosecutor's Exhibit 172 to be shown to the witness in order to have all the necessary precautions, given that this relates to weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the weapon?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All guns are the same to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Earlier on, you were answering questions put by Mr. Par as to the weapon which was at your home, at least when your husband was arrested. As far as you can remember, was that a weapon that looked like this one?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really cannot recollect the appearance of the rifle that we had in our home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Seeing it again doesn't arouse any memories, does it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, usher. I think you can take the document -- the weapon, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Answering questions put by Mr. Par earlier on, you explained that you had insisted for your husband to get this weapon and that you needed the weapon because your husband was off and away and you had to make sure that your children were safe. Doesn't such a thing imply that when this weapon was brought home, it was up to you to be able to use this weapon?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was up to me. But believe me, I have no idea how to use a gun. My brother explained to me the simplest things that needed to be done; to put a bullet in and to cock the gun. I just wanted to have it in the house to be able to frighten the burglar. I really don't know anything about guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you ever use a gun? Did you ever shoot, just for training purposes, of course?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I tried once.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did your husband shoot with the gun?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, no. Maybe at the time of his arrest, he shot twice. I tried, but he wouldn't let me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So you can't remember then that he fired with the gun when he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do remember I tried to shoot, and the rifle that was taken away probably has my fingerprints on it. But I really was confused. I gave the gun to Vlatko. He shot with it twice. He could have killed me and himself, because we thought that they were burglars.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, the night when he was arrested, your husband fired the gun?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he did fire it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who did he aim at?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He fired it at the wall. He thought he would shoot into the air, but it was dark and it hit the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Where was the gun in the house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Behind the door in the bedroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So the weapon was in the bedroom, just behind the door. Was it loaded?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was. I don't remember, actually, whether it was loaded, but I think it was. I can't remember exactly, because when I talk about it, I get upset.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Beforehand, I mean before the night of the arrest in December 1997, prior to that date had your husband used the gun to train with it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not on that day. But when it was purchased in '95, he came home carrying the gun, and he said, "Look what a horrible gun they gave me." He didn't know anything about it, nor did I, but my brother, who works in the warehouse -- and this gun was sometimes in the shop and sometimes in the house, and he explained to us how to handle the gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, although you both didn't know how to use guns, you kept that gun in the room, in the bedroom. It was an AK-47 gun, and it was loaded?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could this weapon be purchased freely? Was it perfectly legal to purchase such a weapon?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We obtained it legally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In other words, you didn't need to have any permit from the administration, any authorisation from any administrative service?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You see, in those days all the institutions were not fully operational, so I really don't understand these things very well. It was only later, after the war, we were all informed that such rifles cannot be kept at home or on the premises because it was illegal. You are allowed to have a pistol, that is, a guard, a security officer may have one, or a hunting rifle is permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you know who your husband purchased the weapon from?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My husband did not buy the gun, but he was regularly issued this gun, which can be seen from the card which was registered and put away in our register in a regular fashion. He didn't buy it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I only have a copy, so I didn't know that that card was yellow. But I'll come to this in a moment. However, could you tell us from whom, if he didn't buy the weapon, from whom he borrowed the gun?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He didn't borrow it either. It says, clearly on the card, that it was issued by Mr. Miljko Omazic, who was working at that time as a keeper and who issued the gun. These were cards that were issued for such weapons. It is a regular document with the weapon indicated, the kind of weapon, who issued it, and to whom it was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Please, madam, could you explain this to me? I didn't quite get it. That person who gave the weapon to your husband, what is that person supposed to do? What is her or his job?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was the keeper of the warehouse. We called them magacioner, the person who issues goods, the person who keeps the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Which warehouse, madam?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it an official warehouse of the administration, government services?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of warehouse it was. I just know that Vlatko went to the brigade and asked whether he could be given something, as I was living alone with his parents, so I really don't know what kind of warehouse it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, at the time and probably also in January 1995, anyone was free to go to the barracks or the warehouse, ask for an AK-47 and get it; is that so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It depended on the reasons that the person would indicate as a reason for requesting a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I shall ask the usher to submit to the witness Defence Exhibit D35/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in saying that this yellow card, it was yellow as the original card, that this card deals with the working hours performed by an employee, a staff member?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a card showing that Vlatko Kupreskic was issued a rifle in 1995, and these were cards that were issued under such occasion. It is clearly stated here who issued the weapon. No working hours are indicated here. Perhaps in those days they didn't have the appropriate forms. That is possible, I don't know, as to the typewritten headings of columns. So it is a kind of receipt card.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who signed this card? A certain Cevozic, do you know this person? Who is this person?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It should say Miljko Omazic [realtime error corrected], Miljko Omazic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: It might be a problem in translation, but what are you reading? "Cevozic", am I wrong in doing so?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: There is a mistake in the English translation. I have the original. It says "Miljko Omazic". So it is an error in the English translation, so could the usher please show the Prosecutor the original card so that he can see for himself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us see it first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: If I understood your explanations well, this card was issued at the very time when your husband was given the weapon, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This card was issued at the same time as the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Allow me to ask the question. Why was he given the card? Is it more customary, when you take a valuable item from a public warehouse, as was the case here, isn't it so that you sign a receipt which is to be filed in the archives of that public warehouse? Would it be more logical for your husband to sign the receipt and to hand it over to the person who issued the weapon to him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know how they kept their records over there. I just know that Vlatko brought with him this card, certifying that he had been issued this weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In this card, we see that your husband was issued three magazines of ammunition. We know where one of them is. Where are the other two, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know how many frames you took away, but I know that one of them was in the shop down there under the counter. Another one, I don't know where it is. And the one that was in the shop, my brother took away when the weapons were handed over, so that I don't have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, shall we have a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thirty minutes' break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Before the adjournment, we were talking about the rifle, AK-47, which your husband was issued in 1995. Will you please tell us whether your husband had, at any time before that, in possession, did he have any rifle, any kind of weapon, before that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Before? I didn't quite get you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: My question related to the period which preceded the moment when he was issued the AK-47.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I must insist on more precision. I'm interested in any kind of weapons; that is, a hunting rifle or whatever. Any kind of weapon.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he never had either a hunting rifle or an airgun.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mrs. Kupreskic, I should like to show you now, with the help of the usher, a document which is called the report on the inventory taken by the inventory commission of the 12th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The first page of the Bosnian version of this document, to the right, we can see the name of Vlatko Kupreskic. Under his name we see a signature. Is this your husband's signature?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now move on to the 15th of April, 1993. Could you please tell us, what do you know about the reasons for and circumstances under which your husband travelled to Croatia on the 14th and 15th of April, 1993, or so it would seem?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The reason why they went there was to purchase some textile goods which they had ordered for a buyer -- or rather for (redacted); and the second reason was that Ankica Kupreskic, Mr. Ivica Kupreskic's wife, was coming back from Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And what was the quantity, how big was this lot of clothes that you brought from that trip?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, usually those textiles were packed in large bags and sacks, and the tennis shoes were in smaller boxes or crates, so that we had just one large bag of jeans, and there was underwear in a smaller bag, and children's sneakers were in a cardboard box. I wouldn't know exactly how many pairs, how many pairs of whatever, but it wasn't a significant quantity, because it was really very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And doesn't one calculate the value of merchandise in the clothing business by the number of pieces, by the number of items? Could you tell us how many items were brought by your husband on that particular occasion when he went on that business trip?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Who could remember that, really? It was to be entered in the books on the next day, but in the morning of the next day the war broke out, so I really can't remember how many items there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: All right. We do not have to talk about the number of items, but could you tell us how many parcels there were?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was one box, and there was this one large bag with jeans. And a slightly smaller bag, a bag smaller than this biggest bag, was the bag with underwear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And how about tennis shoes, sneakers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Children's sneakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: How many, approximately?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And all this was in the boot of the Yugo 45?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, some of it was in the boot and some of this was in the back seats. It fitted in, I mean, it practically all fitted in, in the Yugo 45, all that was brought on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And where was your husband sitting, then? Because you say that the merchandise was in the back seats, so where was your husband sitting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, he couldn't be in the front because only two people could be in front, but I do not remember who sat in the front, whether it was Ankica or Vlatko. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I should like to tell you that Vlatko Kupreskic -- that this -- he never saw this merchandise because it was in the boot, so it says that it was all in the boot, but nobody could see that. Another witness said that he could not see it because it was in the boot. So was it all in the boot of the car?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Will Mr. Usher help me to show the Witness D26/3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us, what is it all about?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This document says that Vlatko Kupreskic is authorised to go on a business trip to Vitez, Split, Vitez, from the 15th of April until the 24th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who issued this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I suppose the authorities. This issue was usually obtained in the municipality, and up here it says the Croatian Defence -- Council of Defence. I don't know, because it wasn't me who went to get this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Why was it issued in the name of Vlatko Kupreskic rather than the owner of the company, Ivica Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, this authorisation was issued on an individual basis, and every person had to have his own authorisation to be able to move about freely. I guess that Ivica Kupreskic also had such an authorisation. I don't really know. I don't know whether he had such a permit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you have the original of the document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't have the original of this document because all the documents were taken away when Vlatko was arrested, and I saw them, with my own eyes, take away all the documents from our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because Mr. Ivica Kupreskic, when he testified here, said that the original of the document that you have now before you was in your possession, and he had given it to you. Of course, he didn't know what you did with it afterwards, but he said that he'd given it to you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never asked Ivica to give me his permit, excuse me. Whether it's in the house or where, in the archives, among the records, in the files, I can't tell you. But all the documents that relate to Vlatko Kupreskic were the originals which were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Are you quite positive about the date of the trip your husband made to Croatia? In other words, are you quite positive that he left on the 14th of April and that he returned on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm 100 per cent certain that he left on the 14th of April and returned on the 15th of April, in late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Are you absolutely positive that the purpose of his trip was only to buy a few pairs of jeans and some other things on the market in Split and, secondly, to meet Mrs. Kupreskic, calling her and giving her a lift from the Split airport? Did he have any other plans for that business trip?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: If he had some other business plans, for instance, to negotiate -- to conduct negotiations about a sale or something, would you have been informed about that, would you know about that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, as a rule, I always know where my husband is. He calls me either by telephone or let's me know in some way or other. Whether he was supposed to conduct some negotiations to strike a deal or something, I really can't remember because it was a long time ago. Whether down there they were about to conclude a business contract or something, I really can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you remember if during that trip, when he was either in Croatia or on his way, did he call you to tell you what was going on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really can't remember. He may have. I was also absent because I also was having additional driving lessons, and I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about the return of your husband on the 15th of April in late afternoon or the evening?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can tell you all that you want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you share your memories? When did he come back, how did he come back, what did he do with the merchandise, and things like that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: So he arrived on the 15th of April, '93, late in the afternoon or early evening, around 7.00. I came out of the house, greeted Mrs. Ankica Kupreskic because I had not seen her for a year and a half. Then those clothes were taken out of the car and into the house, and it was agreed that all this had to be delivered to Travnik the next morning around 8.00. Then they left. We entered our house, and that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: According to several other witnesses who testified here before the Tribunal, that indeed in the house of Ivica Kupreskic there was a kind of a party to celebrate the return of his wife. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember going there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Let us now move to the night between the 15th and 16th of April. Yesterday you told us that at dawn, you received two anonymous telephone calls and a third telephone call which came from Ivica Kupreskic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: At what time did the first anonymous phone call come?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first anonymous telephone call, as far as I can remember, was around 3.00 in the morning, and the second one, around 5.00. So Ivica called shortly after that second anonymous call.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: We need to be accurate about this. There may have been an error, because I heard that this first anonymous call was much later. Are you absolutely certain that this first call, which told you to move to the shelter, came around 3.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was around 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Are you quite sure? You were looking for an explanation -- rather observation made by Mr. Par, and he was asking you about lights in the house, that you must have switched on the lights in order to answer the telephone. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't have any need to light the lights, because it is a custom with us in Bosnia to leave some lights on either at the entrance door or in the passage. In my house, there were two lamps on, so I don't need to. One can see. I do not have any blinds on the windows, so one can see through, and I had no reason to switch the lights on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you remember something more about that person who called you at 3.00 in the morning? What was his exact words?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do remember. He said to go to the shelter because the Muslims would attack us. I asked, "Who is it," and he put down the phone. Because there had been such similar provocations, I just went back to bed and I didn't wake Vlatko up to tell him because he was tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you have such anonymous telephone calls before that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us more specifically when that was?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When? Let me see. But it was sometime between '92 -- at the turn of 1993 from '92. Which month, I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The second call you told us came at 5.00 in the morning. Was it the same voice?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't remember it, really, whether it was the same voice or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did the person who called you at 5.00 in the morning say about the same thing? Was it the same reason, why he called?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: These two telephone calls coming from somebody who told you the same thing twice, didn't they upset you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because they were provocations of that kind so that I wasn't upset. I again went back to bed. Were it not for Ivica Kupreskic to call us again, we would have been caught unawares in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you think that it was impossible that the Muslims would attack Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could never really grasp it, take it into my head, that the Muslims would attack us, our neighbours. It was just beyond me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, your Muslim neighbours. So likewise it would be impossible that the Bosnian army attacks Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if one can imagine such a thing or not, I know nothing about those things, nor could I ever imagine that a conflict could break out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Now I should like to ask you to show us on this aerial photograph, I hope you can identify things on this photograph, the road which you took in the morning of the 16th of April to go from your house to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is our shop (indicating), and here (indicating), I think, should be our house. So we came down from our house by the warehouse to the road which leads to Ivica Kupreskic's house. We passed by Ivica Kupreskic's house here (indicating), towards the woods here (indicating), went through the woods and came out onto the road which passes by Santic's house. Then we proceeded down there to the shelter. Somewhere here (indicating), I think, was the playground, and one could already hear shots fired in Ahmici when we got here. Then we got to this road (indicating). There is a curve here (indicating). And we reached the house of Jelena, the house of Jozo Vrebac.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not hear the end of the witness's sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you please now trace that route on this map which we shall give you in a moment?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 360.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, the photograph that you have in front of you is the same as the one on the easel. The usher is going to give you a marker, a pen, and please trace the path that you have just shown us on the map, on the aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us, madam, that upon arriving near the playground, the sports grounds, you heard the first shots. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you simply put a cross, showing us where that sports playground is that you have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Witness complies) I said that when we reached the sports grounds, we heard it, so it was at this point (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So when you arrived at the spot marked with a cross, on this pass, it was at that point in time that you heard the first shots, just to clarify?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you left your house, you were with your husband, your two children, and according to what you said yesterday, I think, your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you remember how your husband was dressed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, madam?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can. That morning, Vlatko was wearing a velvet chocolate-coloured jacket. It's a short jacket, a winter jacket. And he had corduroy pants in a dark colour, and a shirt, as far as I remember, a chequered shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you left your house, in the area in which you lived, did you see any other people around you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When we reached Niko Sakic's house, I saw Niko Sakic in the yard, and I saw Dragomir Samija in his yard. And then, some 500 metres away, I saw Milan and Mara Samija.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But before reaching those houses, did you see other people? Did you see anybody close to Ivica Kupreskic's house and the house of Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic? Did you see people later on in the woods through which you passed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that upon leaving your house to go towards Ivica Kupreskic's house, you passed by Sakib Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, along the path we took, you could see Sakib Ahmic's house, but it was not by the house that we passed. It doesn't mean that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you think that Sakib Ahmic's family was warned of the need to find shelter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I reached Ivica Kupreskic's house, I saw that the light was switched on in Sakib Ahmic's house, and I remember that very well. Now, whether they had been informed or not, I couldn't tell. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But as you just told us a moment ago that it was customary in Bosnia to leave a light on, what you saw has no meaning?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it does mean, because the light in the house was on. Not outside the house, not light bulbs in front of the door or on the balconies. That I really do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When leaving your house, until you reached your shelter, did you meet or see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't meet anyone, but when I reached Ivica Kupreskic's house, I heard some steps, and it looked like, to me, the echo of certain steps. Now, whether they were soldiers or not, I couldn't see from Ivica Kupreskic's house, but I did hear those steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you speak of these steps, are you thinking of a group of marching soldiers or simply people passing by? I think the distinction can quite easily be made.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't see, so I couldn't tell you what kind of group it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When was it that you decided to go to Mr. Vrebac's house, to the shelter there, and not to any other?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because we went to that shelter before, and when we passed by Niko Sakic's house, he said that it was full and that we should go on, though we had never used Niko's shelter before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I should like to show the witness Exhibit D13/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Will you please look at this document, and as soon as you become familiar with it, I should like you to put it under the ELMO so that we can see what we are looking at. Do we see, in this document given to the Tribunal by the Defence, Mr. Vrebac's house where you found shelter in the course of the day of the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is the house of Jelena, Mr. Jozo Vrebac's daughter. This was the house where we were on the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In the same photo album we can see pictures of the basement of this house. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can you show us the other photographs on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in which part of the basement did you find refuge, by mentioning the number attached to the photograph?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Here, in this part (indicating), which means -- there's another door behind here (indicating), to the left. The number of the picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us which photograph you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Photograph number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Very well. I apologise for interrupting you. What were you saying about what is shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Behind here, there's another door and another room. There's a room here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Very well. In this album, can we see the room which you took shelter in when you arrived on the 16th of April, 1993, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Here, in the corner here. You can't see it on this photograph, this photograph number 4. It's here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And you can't see that room on any other photograph in the album?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The steps, and these are parts of the staircase, but I don't see this room on any of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you turn the page and show the witness other photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Looking at these photographs, 5, 6, and 7, do you recognise the room in which you took shelter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the room, shown on number 6 (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So it is the room that is opened by the door in the middle of this photograph, number 6; could you tell us whether you spent the whole day in that room?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't spend the whole day in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left this room?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA KUPRESKIC (Resumed)
